construction_markdown: No new leaderboard code is submitted. The audited multilevel family has 32,768 blocks of length 32,768 and full inner space `B_0=RM(1,15)`. Fix a strict binary-linear flag `B_0 ⊋ B_1 ⊋ ... ⊋ B_s=0`. Put `m_i=dim(B_i)-dim(B_{i+1})`, choose a linear complement section `σ_i:F_2^{m_i}→B_i`, and choose a binary-linear outer constituent `E_i≤(F_2^{m_i})^{32768}` of dimension `κ_i`. Encode `(e_i)_i` blockwise by `c_j=Σ_i σ_i(e_{i,j})`. The result proves an exact ceiling of 1,040 for the standard first-active-level product certificate, a sharper ceiling of 996 when the repetition line is isolated, and a universal ceiling of 1,054 for arbitrary binary-linear coupling whose block projections have rank at most 16.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For a flag `B_i` with sections `σ_i`, define `ω_i(u)=min_{v∈B_{i+1}} wt(σ_i(u)+v)`. If `E_i` is the level-`i` outer code, then first-active-level decoding gives `d(C)≥min_i min_{e∈E_i\{0}} Σ_j ω_i(e_j)`. Hence `d(C)≥min_i Δ_i λ_i`, where `λ_i=min_{u≠0}ω_i(u)`. This weighted-shell statement cleanly identifies where ordinary product-distance analysis loses information.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem and scope

Let `T=535822336`, and partition the final coordinates into `N=32768` blocks of length `L=32768`.

1. Every full `RM(1,15)` generalized concatenation whose distance is certified by the standard first-active-level shell-product bound has dimension at most 1,040. If the repetition line is isolated as its own level, the stronger bound is 996.
2. Every binary-linear code with this block partition and block-projection ranks at most 16 has dimension at most 1,054, regardless of cross-level coupling.
3. The shared degree-64 RS–RM code admits no strict additive supercode using the same coordinatewise affine inner map.

These are scoped obstructions, not an upper bound for arbitrary binary-linear codes.

## 1. Linearity, dimension, and the weighted-shell bound

Let

`B_0 ⊋ B_1 ⊋ ... ⊋ B_s=0`, with `B_0=RM(1,15)`,

and choose complements `B_i=σ_i(F_2^{m_i}) ⊕ B_{i+1}`. Let `E_i≤(F_2^{m_i})^N` be binary linear of dimension `κ_i`. The blockwise sum of the sections is binary linear. Uniqueness of the direct-sum decomposition in every block makes the encoder injective, so

`dim C=Σ_i κ_i`.

For a quotient symbol define

`ω_i(u)=min_{v∈B_{i+1}} wt(σ_i(u)+v)`, with `ω_i(0)=0`.

For `e∈E_i`, put `W_i(e)=Σ_j ω_i(e_j)`. If level `i` is the first active level of a nonzero encoded word, every later contribution in block `j` belongs to `B_{i+1}`. That block therefore has weight at least `ω_i(e_j)`. Hence

`d(C)≥min_i min_{e∈E_i\{0}} W_i(e)`.

If `Δ_i` is the block distance of `E_i` and `λ_i=min_{u≠0}ω_i(u)`, this implies the standard product certificate

`d(C)≥min_i Δ_i λ_i`. 

## 2. Shells of `RM(1,15)`

A nonzero affine truth table has weight 16,384 unless it is the constant-one word, which has weight 32,768. Therefore every nonempty shell `B_i\B_{i+1}` has minimum weight 16,384, except the unique possible shell `Rep\{0}`, where `Rep=<1>` and the weight is 32,768. Indeed, a shell with minimum 32,768 can contain only the all-one word, forcing `B_i=Rep` and `B_{i+1}=0`.

Suppose first that `Rep` is not isolated. Under the standard product certificate, every level must satisfy

`Δ_i·16384≥T`, so `Δ_i≥32704`.

Puncturing any `Δ_i-1` outer block positions is injective on `E_i`. The remaining 65 positions contain at most `65m_i` binary coordinates, whence

`κ_i≤65m_i`.

Since `Σ_i m_i=dim RM(1,15)=16`,

`dim C≤65·16=1040`.

If `Rep` is isolated, the other quotient dimensions sum to 15 and contribute at most 975. The repetition-level outer constituent must be a binary code of length 32,768 and distance at least

`T/32768=16352`.

The next section bounds its dimension by 21, yielding

`dim C≤975+21=996`.

The shared outer `[32768,65,32704]_{2^16}` concatenated with `RM(1,15)` attains the 1,040 ceiling, so the first bound is exact within its stated certificate class.

## 3. A self-contained cubic Delsarte bound

Let `n_0=32768`, `d_0=a=16352`, `t=n_0-2a=64`, and `z=n_0-2x`. Define

`F(x)=(a-x)(tz+n_0)^2`.

For every integer `x≥d_0`, `F(x)≤0`. With binary Krawtchouk polynomials

`K_0=1`, `K_1=z`, `K_2=(z^2-n_0)/2`,

`K_3=(z^3-(3n_0-2)z)/6`,

the exact expansion `F=Σ_{j=0}^3 f_jK_j` has

`f_0=30064771072`, `f_1=603975680`,

`f_2=3932160`, `f_3=12288`.

All coefficients are positive.

For any binary code `A` of size `M`, define its normalized distance distribution

`A_x=M^{-1}|{(u,v)∈A^2:d(u,v)=x}|`.

Character orthogonality gives, for every `j`,

`Σ_x A_xK_j(x)=M^{-1} Σ_{wt(y)=j} |Σ_{u∈A}(-1)^{u·y}|^2≥0`.

Thus

`Σ_x A_xF(x)≥f_0M`.

If the minimum distance is at least `d_0`, all nonzero occurring distances have `F(x)≤0`, while `A_0=1`. Therefore

`f_0M≤F(0)=74181816143052800`,

and consequently

`M≤F(0)/f_0=2467400<2^22`.

For a linear code `M=2^c`, so `c≤21`.

## 4. Arbitrary coupling: the 1,054 ceiling

Let `C` now be any binary-linear code of length `2^30`, partitioned into 32,768 blocks of length 32,768, and suppose every block projection of `C` has rank at most 16. Fix any 65 blocks and shorten `C` by requiring all of them to be zero. These requirements have total codimension at most `65·16=1040`, so the shortened subcode `C'` has dimension

`s≥dim C-1040`.

Delete the 65 zero blocks. Dimension and minimum distance are unchanged, while the residual length is

`n'=32703·32768=1071611904`.

For a binary code of size `M` and distance at least `T`, summing ordered-pair distances gives

`M(M-1)T≤n'M^2/2`,

because at each coordinate at most `M^2/2` ordered pairs differ. Since `2T>n'`,

`M≤2T/(2T-n')=32704<2^15`.

For the linear residual code `M=2^s`, hence `s≤14`. Combining this with `s≥dim C-1040` proves

`dim C≤1054`.

This argument permits arbitrary binary-additive outer spaces, coordinate-dependent inner copies, and global cross-level coupling. It only uses the rank-16 bound on each displayed block.

## 5. The existing 1,040-dimensional code cannot be additively extended

Use the explicit field and evaluation set from the shared construction:

`F=F_2[α]/(α^16+α^5+α^3+α^2+1)`,

`A=span{1,α,...,α^14}`,

and let `D_0` be evaluation on `A` of all polynomials of degree at most 64. For the affine inner encoder `H`,

`wt(H^A(u))=2^14(32768-N_0(u)+N_1(u))`.

Thus the target is exactly `N_0(u)-N_1(u)≤64`.

The shared reciprocal-sum lemma proves additive maximality as follows. If `v∉D_0`, fix a 64-set `R⊂A`, interpolate `v` on `R` by a polynomial `h_R` of degree at most 63, and let `G_R=∏_{r∈R}(X-r)`. The pencil

`u_t=v+ev_A(h_R+tG_R)`, for `t∈F`,

has 64 forced zeros. The target inequality says that its additional zero count is at most its one count. Summing over all `t`, each coordinate outside `R` contributes once to each count, so equality must hold for every `t`. Equality of the corresponding parameter multisets forces

`Σ_{x∈A\R} G_R(x)^{-1}=0`.

For the explicit set

`R=(span{1,α,...,α^5}\{0})∪{α^6}`,

the exact subspace-polynomial computation in the shared proof gives reciprocal sum `0x0990≠0`. This contradiction shows that every strict additive outer supercode of `D_0` contains a word below the target. Hence the familiar dimension-1,040 code cannot be enlarged while retaining this fixed affine inner encoder.

proof_steps.proof: The chosen complements form a direct-sum decomposition of every inner block. The blockwise encoder is binary linear and injective, so dimensions of the independent outer constituents add.
proof_steps.statement: The generalized-concatenation code is binary linear and has dimension `Σ_i κ_i`.

proof_steps.proof: For the first active level, every later contribution lies in the next inner subcode. Minimizing over that subcode gives the coset weight `ω_i`, and summing over blocks proves the weighted bound.
All nonconstant affine words have weight 16,384; the only nonzero affine word of larger weight is the constant-one word. A shell containing only that word must be `Rep\{0}`.
proof_steps.statement: Every flag shell has minimum 16,384 except the isolated repetition shell, whose minimum is 32,768.

proof_steps.proof: The product certificate forces outer block distance at least 32,704. Puncturing 32,703 block positions is injective, leaving 65 symbols of `m_i` bits.
proof_steps.statement: An ordinary quotient level contributes at most `65m_i` binary dimensions.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed polynomial is nonpositive on every allowed nonzero distance and has four positive Krawtchouk coefficients. Character-sum positivity gives `M≤F(0)/f_0=2,467,400`, hence linear dimension at most 21.
Without an isolated repetition shell, the 16 quotient bits each cost at most 65 dimensions. With it isolated, the other 15 bits contribute at most 975 and the repetition constituent at most 21.
proof_steps.statement: The standard full-RM flag ceiling is 1,040; the isolated-repetition ceiling is 996.

proof_steps.proof: Shortening 65 rank-16 blocks loses at most 1,040 dimensions. The residual code has length 1,071,611,904 and distance at least 535,822,336; Plotkin bounds its size by 32,704, so its binary dimension is at most 14.
proof_steps.statement: Every arbitrarily coupled rank-16-block code at the target has dimension at most 1,054.

proof_steps.proof: The interpolation-pencil lemma would force every 64-point reciprocal sum to vanish, while the explicit shared set gives `0x0990`.
proof_steps.statement: The shared degree-64 RS outer space has no strict additive supercode under its fixed affine inner encoder.

theorem_statement: For generalized concatenation through the full inner code `RM(1,15)`, every independent flag construction certified by the standard first-active-level shell-product bound has dimension at most 1,040; isolating the repetition line lowers the ceiling to 996. More generally, every binary-linear code split into 32,768 length-32,768 blocks whose block projections have rank at most 16 has dimension at most 1,054 at the immutable distance. The existing dimension-1,040 degree-64 RS–RM code also has no strict additive outer supercode under its fixed affine inner encoder. No new leaderboard code is produced.
title: Multilevel RM-block ceilings: 1,040 standard and 1,054 fully coupled
